data.name: Bellatia
data.detailed_description:
Oferta especial


  • The Art of Bellatia, an official PDF sourcebook including Bellatia's artwork(total 44 pages), will be placed in your Steam folder:
..\Steam\SteamApps\common\Bellatia\Digital Extras\


Acerca do jogo

Bellatia is a hack 'n' slash action role-playing game about warriors fighting over the ultimate godly weapon called the 'Bellatia' in the land of Aslan.

The dark magic wizard Khadal is trying to take over the world by collecting the power of all the heroes of the past. When the great wizard Arkreign learns of this plan, he overthrows it by locking the heroes' powers in many Bellastones and scattering them all over the world. No one knows what happened to Khadal and Arkreign afterward and the existence of the Bellastones has become a myth, dividing the warriors into two groups.

First is those seeking to free the Bellatia souls and the other is those who want the power for themselves. The ones who are not capable of handling the power of Bellatia are turning into evil beings and causing much turmoil in the world.

A girl is the last hope for mankind and the player must train the girl, interact with the bygone heroes to draw out their power, stop the evil from resurrecting, and restore peace in the world.

Features

  • Deep combat mechanics that requires strategy and skills : Every boss comes with unique traits and attack patterns. Master the combat style for each weapon type and take on the enemy!
  • Fascinating action : Enjoy fast and exhilarating action against numerous monsters. Well-managing your equipment and timely use of the berserker mode and Bellatia is key!
  • Various equipment and charming weapons : Upgrade various swords, spears, wands, and two-hand swords to prevail over the enemy. Strategically utilize the weapon's property advantage in combat for more effectiveness.
  • Special attacks : Use the different berserker skill for each weapon and the rush skill to unleash attacks non-stop and dominate the battle!

reviews.review:
Bellatia is a fantasy hack-and-slash action RPG developed by Ganitani and published by H2 Interactive Co., Ltd. The game places most of its attention on fast combat, character progression, equipment management, and battles against increasingly dangerous enemies. Rather than attempting to compete with enormous open-world RPGs, it delivers a more concentrated adventure built around defeating groups of monsters, obtaining better equipment, mastering different weapons, and learning how to use the protagonist's supernatural abilities effectively. Its anime-influenced visual direction and straightforward structure give it the character of a smaller-scale action RPG, although its modest production values are noticeable throughout the experience.

The story takes place in the land of Aslan and revolves around a mysterious source of power called Bellatia. Long before the protagonist's journey begins, the dark wizard Khadal attempted to gather the abilities of legendary heroes so that he could dominate the world. Another powerful wizard, Arkreign, opposed him and ultimately sealed these heroic powers inside objects known as Bellastones before scattering them throughout the land. Both wizards eventually vanished, leaving the Bellastones and the extraordinary forces contained within them to become part of history and legend. It is a conventional fantasy setup, but the idea of ancient heroic powers becoming dangerous objects of desire gives the setting a reasonably interesting foundation.

The situation becomes more complicated as warriors begin searching for Bellatia. Some seek to release the souls connected to this ancient power, while others want to claim it for themselves. Bellatia is also inherently dangerous because individuals unable to control its influence can become corrupted monsters. The protagonist, a young female warrior, becomes central to preventing another catastrophe. Her journey involves becoming stronger, encountering the lingering influence of past heroes, fighting corrupted creatures, and confronting those who would misuse Bellatia. The premise contains enough mythology to establish a sense of purpose, although storytelling is secondary to combat. Players looking for elaborate conversations, extensive role-playing choices, or complex character relationships will find the narrative relatively simple.

Combat provides the game's strongest reason to continue. Bellatia offers several weapon categories, including swords, spears, wands, and two-handed swords. Each provides a different approach to attacking enemies, allowing players to experiment until they discover a style that suits them. Weapons are not merely cosmetic alternatives because their characteristics can affect their usefulness against particular opponents. Equipment can also be upgraded, creating a familiar but effective progression cycle in which fighting enemies leads to stronger equipment that prepares the protagonist for more difficult encounters.

Special abilities add another layer to the fighting. Different weapons are associated with Berserker abilities, while the Rush mechanic helps maintain aggressive offensive sequences. Bellatia powers can also be incorporated into battle, making timing an important consideration when facing tougher enemies. When these mechanics work together, combat becomes more engaging than simple button mashing. Deciding when to activate powerful abilities, which weapon to equip, and how aggressively to approach an enemy gives the player some tactical control without making the system unnecessarily complicated.

Boss encounters make better use of these mechanics because individual bosses possess recognizable characteristics and attack patterns. Learning those patterns and responding appropriately provides some of Bellatia's more satisfying moments. Charging forward without paying attention can quickly become ineffective, so observation and positioning have greater importance during major encounters. Unfortunately, ordinary battles do not consistently provide the same degree of excitement. Fighting repeated groups of enemies can eventually become predictable, and the limited variety makes the basic gameplay loop feel repetitive during longer sessions.

Character and equipment progression partially compensate for this repetition. Improving weapons and experimenting with their different properties provides a continuing incentive to engage with battles. The game succeeds at creating a simple cycle of combat, rewards, upgrades, and stronger opposition. It never develops into an exceptionally deep role-playing system, but it contains enough customization to distinguish itself from a completely linear action game. Players who enjoy gradually improving a character and testing upgraded equipment against stronger monsters will probably get more from Bellatia than those primarily interested in exploration or storytelling.

The visual presentation uses a colorful fantasy aesthetic with clear anime influences. Character designs, magical effects, monsters, and weapons fit the supernatural setting well, and the female protagonist has a distinctive appearance that helps establish the game's identity. However, the overall presentation reveals the project's limited scale. Environments can appear sparse, animations are not always especially fluid, and some areas lack the visual detail needed to make Aslan feel like a fully developed fantasy world. The graphics are functional and occasionally attractive, but they rarely become a major attraction by themselves.

Bellatia's greatest problem is therefore not a complete absence of worthwhile ideas, but the inconsistent refinement of those ideas. Multiple weapon types, equipment upgrades, Berserker attacks, Bellatia abilities, enemy properties, and pattern-driven bosses provide a respectable foundation. The game clearly understands the appeal of an action RPG progression loop. What holds it back is repetitive encounter design and a general lack of polish. Combat can be enjoyable when its various systems are working together, yet movement, feedback, animations, and encounter variety do not consistently provide the responsiveness expected from stronger hack-and-slash games.

Despite these shortcomings, Bellatia can still appeal to a specific audience. Players interested in smaller fantasy action RPGs, anime-inspired character designs, equipment progression, and uncomplicated hack-and-slash combat may find several enjoyable qualities here. It is relatively easy to understand, provides several ways to approach combat, and offers enough progression to encourage experimentation. Its fantasy mythology also gives the fighting some narrative context even though the story never becomes the primary attraction.

Overall, Bellatia is an ambitious but noticeably rough action RPG that contains more mechanical variety than its modest presentation initially suggests. Its assortment of weapons, upgrade systems, special abilities, Bellatia mechanics, and boss patterns creates an entertaining foundation, but repetitive battles and limited polish prevent the experience from becoming exceptional. Players willing to overlook those limitations can find a reasonably enjoyable fantasy adventure centered on combat and progression, while anyone expecting sophisticated storytelling or highly refined action may come away disappointed. 

Rating: 5/10
